changes.title: A real menu bar and two clear buttons at the top
changes.why: Now there is no way to move around or order from the top, and the only link is a tiny underlined line; a site needs a menu with an Order button and a basket count (website, not a page).

changes.title: Every loaf gets an Add button with its price
changes.why: Now the counter is only a gallery, so a customer cannot pick anything; each item gets one clear button, and bigger prices and notes so they read at a glance.

changes.title: A basket where each line can be changed or removed
changes.why: Now nothing can be chosen at all; the basket shows each item with plus, minus and a bin, the total, and how much more is needed for delivery (from your own 120 shekel rule).

changes.title: Ordering in three short steps: basket, when and where, details
changes.why: Now the order button goes nowhere; one question per screen, a button that names the next step, and a Back button, as the page rules ask for every order.

changes.title: The top bar stays readable on a phone, with a basket bar below
changes.why: Now the page words run through the name and clock when you scroll; a solid bar fixes it, and a bottom bar shows what is in the basket.

changes.title: A phone menu panel with pages, and bigger buttons on the opening
changes.why: Now the phone shows only a clock and a language button; a Menu button opens the pages, and the opening gets two easy-to-press buttons instead of a small link.

changes.title: The last button finally works, and the footer has links
changes.why: Now Message the bakery points back to the top of the page and the footer text is tiny; the button starts the order and the footer links to the sections.

changes.title: Visit details bigger, with an Open in Maps link
changes.why: Now the labels and facts are small and the address cannot be tapped; bigger text and a map link make the visit step easy.

questions: What WhatsApp number or phone should orders go to? Right now the order opens WhatsApp so the customer picks the chat.
Can the customer choose a pickup day and time freely, or are there limits (for example no same-day orders, or different times on Friday)?
Is there a delivery fee, or is delivery free above 120 shekels?
Do you want the page in Hebrew as well? The Hebrew button only flips the direction today and the words stay English.
Is Batya the name you want on the page, and may we use Batya's photo or a photo of the real shopfront?
Are the four items the full range, and can a customer order more than one challah or box in a single order, or is there a limit?
checks_now: Real site: no broken links or layout shifts, but tiny tap targets (name, counter link) on a phone, and with motion switched off the headline and opening text stay hidden; no order path at all.
